text:
The text contains significant bias in the second sentence, which makes a subjective and hyperbolic claim about Isaac Asimov's literary status. The phrase "no other author has ever come close to the genius" is an absolute statement that ignores the contributions and critical acclaim of numerous other science fiction authors, such as Arthur C. Clarke, Ursula K. Le Guin, or Frank Herbert. This reflects a subjective opinion presented as objective fact.

Additionally, the claim that modern writers "merely dance around the edges" dismisses the innovation and literary merit of contemporary science fiction, implying that all work after Asimov is inferior or derivative. This is a form of recency bias and elitism, favoring a specific historical figure while devaluing current literary achievements.

The first part of the text, regarding the Great Barrier Reef, is factual and neutral, containing no bias.
